xian-weiyang-xinjiamiao-resettlement.whole: The loan improved six road corridors in Xi'an and upgraded three more roads, about 12 kilometres of each, and put eight new interchanges in place of roundabouts on the First and Second Ring Roads against a target of four. It installed an area traffic control system at 200 junctions, built four bus terminals and depots, and recreated about 8.4 kilometres of Han Dynasty roads in the Weiyang Palace area. By the completion report's count, vehicle speed on the project's key corridors rose from 12 to 45 kilometres an hour against a target of 20, and the number of vehicles receiving emissions testing reached 2,500 against a target of 500. Three rows of the same table came in under target: average speed on Xi Dajie reached 21 kilometres an hour against 25, bus maintenance days 135 against 163, and training and study tours 15 against 18; the plan to reduce vehicle emissions was delivered 3.3 years late and the Han road network 1.5 years late. Works were dropped along the way: Dongcheng Road in Huxian, a 26.7-kilometre bicycle route in the Ming Walled City, intersection channelling, accident remedial measures, road-user education and the strategic urban transport studies. The number of bus priority lanes fell from 13 planned to 1 built, with the report saying the rest were built with local money, and the cultural heritage component was cut by 58 per cent at the 2014 restructuring. The report gives an economic rate of return of 33 per cent at closing, covering 71 per cent of project cost, against 14 per cent at appraisal covering 56 per cent, and says data were extremely scarce at both points; it rated efficiency Substantial for the restructured project and Modest for the original, while the Independent Evaluation Group rated efficiency Modest. Spending came to US$398.0 million against US$458.1 million estimated at appraisal, with the US$150 million loan fully disbursed and the borrower putting in US$248.0 million of the US$308.1 million planned. All of these figures are the lender's own, from its completion report and the Evaluation Group's review of it; no independent check was found.

wuhan-nanhu-village-resettlement-delay.whole: The project built 13.29 kilometres of the three road links it financed against a target of 13.65 — 3.40 kilometres of Shuidong Road, 0.89 of the Shuidong section of the Second Ring Road and 9.00 of Jiefang Avenue against 9.36 planned. It also installed 224 area traffic control junctions, 15.5 kilometres of bus priority corridors, two bus depots, two bus terminals, 46 bus stops made accessible to vulnerable users, 28.4 kilometres of road safety corridors, 48 pedestrian-phase traffic signals against a target of 38, 17 converted mid-block crossings against 9, and 13.3 kilometres of separation between motorised and non-motorised traffic, and delivered 1,200 person-days of training against 1,000. By the completion report's count the average number of deaths a year on the four road safety corridors fell from 22 to 10 against a target of 18, and peak-hour travel time on the Shuidong section fell from 22 minutes to 5 against a target of 15. Rows that fell short: peak-hour bus travel time on Heping Avenue was 33 minutes against a 30-minute target, which the report attributes to road capacity lost to the construction of metro line 5; pedestrian-phase signals on Hanyang Avenue reached 8 against 10; the bus-stop accessibility target was cut from 100 to 96.5 per cent; and Heping Avenue was built 2.7 kilometres shorter than planned. Fifteen activities proposed at appraisal were cancelled during implementation: two public transport corridors on Jiefang Avenue and Xinhua Lu/Youyi Lu, three road safety corridors on Jiefang, Yanhe/Yanjiang and Longyang Avenues, the two public transport terminals at Gangdu Garden and the Jinyintan Park and Ride, dropped over land regulation and counterpart funds for land and demolition not being paid on time, and a study on urban-rural integration. The project cost US$926.8 million against US$610.71 million estimated at appraisal, a 52 per cent rise, with the loan fully disbursed. The report puts the economic rate of return at 17.28 per cent at completion against 15.3 per cent at appraisal, covering the components that account for 97 per cent of the investment, and both the report and the Independent Evaluation Group rated efficiency Modest. Every figure here is the lender's own; no independent check was found.

qingyang-xifeng-ring-road-relocation.whole: The project rehabilitated 16.11 kilometres of urban road against a target of 16.06 and built 5.74 kilometres against 5.76, covering the west and east ring roads, Guxiang Road, Anding Xi Road, the Nan Bei and Anding Dong Xi upgrade and three slow-traffic streets in the old city centre, and built a wastewater treatment plant with its collectors and pumping station. By the completion report's count the share of the built-up area served by storm water and wastewater networks rose from 50.6 to 92 per cent, meeting its target; bus speed in the rush hour on the Nan Bei Street corridor reached 26.9 kilometres an hour against a target of 15.5 from a baseline of 10.3; rush-hour bus ridership on that corridor reached 12,700 against 12,000; 47 bus stops were rebuilt against 33, 194 zebra crossings were signalised against 103 and 28 intersections were channelled against 27; deaths and serious injuries on the project corridors fell to 6 a year against a target of 9 from a baseline of 14; 189 staff were trained against 110 and five studies were completed. The report's journey-time row for through freight traffic gives 28.4 minutes at baseline, a target of 18.2 and 15.8 at completion. The three pollution rows exceeded targets rewritten in 2018 but came to roughly half the targets set at appraisal: 576.5 tonnes a year of biochemical oxygen demand removed against a revised 365 and an original 1,168, 1,631 tonnes of chemical oxygen demand against a revised 802 and an original 2,569, and 1,166 tonnes of suspended solids against a revised 693 and an original 2,219. The targets were cut to match the plant's actual capacity, which the report says had been miscalculated, and the plant was finished two years late. The last kilometre of the Western Ring Road and the purchase of vehicle equipment were cancelled at the 2016 restructuring to ease the pressure on counterpart funding. The report puts the economic rate of return at 13.78 per cent at closing against 12.38 per cent at appraisal, covering 82.4 per cent of cost at closing and 68.3 at appraisal, with the Urban Bypass Road falling from 11.10 to 10.82 per cent in the same table; both the report and the Independent Evaluation Group rated efficiency Modest. The user satisfaction figure of 72 per cent against a 65 per cent target comes from surveys run under the project, and every other figure here is the lender's own; no independent check was found.

xining-wusixi-road-demolition.whole: The project built Xicheng Avenue, the west extension of Wusixi Road and Road No. 5, and upgraded Qiyi, Delingha, Bayi and Wuyi Roads, all recorded at 100 per cent of their revised quantities. By the completion report's count it also improved 61 bus stops against a target of 56, built 46 bus priority junctions against a revised target of 34, bought 145 electric buses, installed 73 bus charging stations and 1,648 on-board units, upgraded 53 signalised junctions against a revised 43, installed 126 image-forensic enforcement systems against a revised 111 and 93 high-definition video monitoring systems against 70, completed five technical studies and trained 979 officials and technical staff against a target of 250. Two headline measures were met only after their targets were relaxed at the 2019 restructuring. Morning peak travel time for public transport users on the corridor came in at 32.77 minutes against a revised target of 33, where the appraisal target had been 15.40 from a baseline of 35.23. Public transport beneficiaries reached 669,768 person-trips against a revised target of 640,000, where the appraisal target had been 704,000. Deaths and serious injuries on Wusixi Road fell to 1 a year against a revised target of 3 from a baseline of 4, and 85.3 per cent of users said they were satisfied, against a revised 85 per cent target, measured by a survey run for the project. Two access roads, Guihua 1 and Guihua 2, were dropped when the public transport interchange moved to Wangjiazhai; some traffic enforcement equipment, including portable recorders, was dropped; and three studies on bus route optimisation, transit metropolis and parking strategy were dropped because they were already being done with counterpart funds. The report puts the economic rate of return at 15.85 per cent at completion against 16.1 per cent at appraisal, covering 93 and 94 per cent of project cost, and attributes the fall to the longer implementation period and to lower traffic during the pandemic, giving 16.68 per cent for a scenario without it. About US$15.5 million of savings was reallocated to extra works, and the closing date was put back 23 months. Both the report and the Independent Evaluation Group rated efficiency Substantial and the outcome Satisfactory. All these figures are the lender's own; no independent check was found.

shangrao-sanqingshan-airport-land-take.whole: The loan paid for the airport itself: a 4C-level airfield with runway and taxiway, the terminal building and apron, the air traffic control building and tower, a freight facility, service vehicles, a storm water reuse system and a ground power unit for parked aircraft. The airport opened on 28 May 2017. By the completion report's count it handled 1,634 take-offs and landings and 146,700 passengers in the seven months to 31 December 2017 and 4,512 and 375,000 in 2018, with 5.4 tonnes of cargo in the first period and 121.2 in the second; average occupancy was 81 per cent and then 77.8 per cent of seats. Travel time between Shangrao and major cities fell 45 per cent against a target of 27 per cent, and the terminal received an EDGE green building certificate on 21 January 2019 on savings of 24 per cent of energy, 42 per cent of water and 38 per cent of embodied energy in materials, the project's second and last objective indicator. The airport infrastructure cost US$121.5 million against US$100.7 million estimated at appraisal: the terminal went from US$10.71 million to US$25.60 million when the municipality decided to build two storeys instead of one, and site preparation from US$13.54 million to US$23.03 million on harder ground than expected and on the larger site, a reason the Independent Evaluation Group says the report does not set out. Construction finished about a year early, the loan closed on its original date and was fully disbursed. The report puts the economic rate of return at 17.84 per cent at completion against 17.13 per cent at appraisal, covering 93 per cent of project cost, and the financial rate of return at 8.54 per cent, with the central aviation fund paying operating and interest subsidies and the municipality committing RMB 27 million of operating subsidy in 2017 and 2018. All of these figures are the lender's own, from its completion report and the Evaluation Group's review of it; no independent check was found.

corridor-x-dimitrovgrad-bypass-serbia.whole: The loan paid for 37.9 kilometres of the E-75 against a revised target of 37.7 and 8.3 kilometres of the E-80 around Dimitrovgrad against a target of 9, which the completion report treats as met because the length was settled by the final design. The Bank-financed works cost EUR 263.06 million against an appraisal estimate of EUR 270.53 million, the Dimitrovgrad bypass coming in at EUR 91.85 million against EUR 93.53 million. By the report's count, road user costs on Niš–Dimitrovgrad fell to EUR 1.00 per vehicle-kilometre, 23 per cent below the baseline; the rate of deaths and serious injuries fell from 44.13 to 33.05 on that section and from 53.34 to 19.12 on the E-75 sections; 312 grievances about the delivery of project benefits were recorded as addressed, all of those registered; and 36,161 person-months of work for local people were created under the contractors against a target of 20,000. Traffic in 2018 came to 70 per cent of the appraisal forecast across the four sections and 46 per cent on the Dimitrovgrad bypass, the report attributing this to the motorways not being fully open until 2019 and to the economic downturn in neighbouring countries. The ex-post economic rate of return for the bypass was 2.6 per cent against 5.9 per cent at appraisal, the lowest of the four sections and the only one below the 6 per cent threshold the report uses; for the project as a whole it was 10.2 per cent against 12.5 per cent, and the toll-based financial rate of return for the whole of Corridor X, including sections other lenders paid for, 12.8 per cent against 15.0 per cent. The Independent Evaluation Group's review reports the 46 per cent figure as the project-wide traffic shortfall, where the report gives it for the E-80 alone. The project ran 10 years against the 6.5 planned; the Dimitrovgrad bypass opened to traffic on 16 September 2017 and was completed on 30 November 2019 after two contract terminations and remedial works for the landslide at Gradinje. Both the report and the Evaluation Group rated efficiency Substantial. These are the lender's own figures; no independent check of them was found.

milot-rreshen-road-compensation-albania.whole: The loan built 26 kilometres of two-lane highway between Milot and Rrëshen in three contracts of 9, 9 and 8 kilometres, all open to traffic by April 2011. By the completion report's count the journey from Rrëshen to Milot in free-flowing conditions fell from 43 minutes to 18–20, a cut of 53 to 58 per cent against a target of 25 per cent; the population living within 20 minutes of Milot rose by about 50 per cent; four performance-based maintenance contracts were signed in the two pilot regions against a target of two contracts; a road safety audit covered 178 lane-kilometres against a target of 120; and the Maritime Administration was set up after the Maritime Code was approved in September 2010. Against that, the improvement in average road condition in the pilot regions reached 4.5 against a target of 10, which the report marks partially achieved and for which it gives no reason; the purchase of 20 pieces of road safety equipment was cancelled at the May 2010 restructuring and six traffic counters and classifiers at the October 2010 restructuring, and nothing was spent on the project unit's vehicles or on training. The report puts the economic rate of return at 24.6 per cent at completion against 19.6 per cent at appraisal, attributing the rise to traffic in 2011 running 32 per cent above the appraisal estimate and to lower construction costs. Its two annexes do not agree on those costs: the economic annex gives US$38.7 million against an appraisal estimate of US$41.0 million for the road, 6 per cent lower, while the cost annex gives US$38.44 million for the three construction lots against US$36.2 million estimated, about 6 per cent higher. The Independent Evaluation Group rated efficiency Substantial and the outcome Satisfactory. All of these figures are the lender's own; no independent check was found.

amman-development-corridor-land.whole: Of the 40-kilometre first phase of the Amman Ring Road, two sections were finished and opened to traffic in February 2012: 13.4 kilometres of dual carriageway with one interchange and one overpass, and 8 kilometres in two short stretches with two interchanges and three overpasses. The third, 18.5 kilometres with two major interchanges and four overpasses, was 65 per cent built when the loan closed and was expected in October 2014, leaving physical completion of the phase at 84 per cent against a target of 100. The new customs depot at Madounah was not built at all, so its indicator stood at zero; 8 kilometres of access roads to sub-grade level, 27 hectares of parking, drainage, a water pipe and an electrical connection were built at the site and left waiting for it. The project's own outcome measures moved the wrong way or short: the cost of moving a container from the Qualifying Industrial Zone to Aqaba port was US$425 at closing against a target of US$300 and a baseline of US$385, which the report sets against a rise in oil prices it estimates at 250 per cent over the same years; travel time from the airport to Zarqa was 48 minutes against a 40-minute target and a 60-minute baseline; and traffic diverted from urban streets reached 8 per cent against 10. The master plans and studies for phases 2 and 3 were delivered, paid for by European Investment Bank and IFC money rather than the loan. The road component cost US$278.87 million against US$106.92 million at appraisal, which the Independent Evaluation Group attributes to fuel and material costs, inflation and failed first bidding, and the Group records the inland port and customs component as practically dropped. The report recalculated the economic rate of return at 12.71 per cent, against 17.5 per cent in the 2004 appraisal — the Group prints that figure as 17.3 per cent — and against 12.73 per cent in an August 2008 update; the borrower's own section of the same report gives 13.07 per cent. These are all the lender's and the borrower's figures; no independent check was found.

lagos-brt-ikorodu-market-traders.whole: The project rebuilt the Mile 12 to Ikorodu road from four lanes to six with segregated bus lanes down the middle, rehabilitated eight bridges on it, upgraded 44 bus shelters on the older Mile 12–CMS corridor and built the Ikeja bus terminal; 17.05 kilometres of road were rehabilitated against a target of 17.8, being the 13.5-kilometre corridor plus 3.55 kilometres of Akin Adesola and Wempco Roads. Bus rapid transit services began in November 2015, running 24 hours a day. By the completion report's count, travel time from Ikorodu to Tafawa Balewa Square fell from 120 minutes to 87 against a 90-minute target, bus speed reached 23 kilometres an hour against 18, direct beneficiaries came to 440,000 against a target of 300,000, of them 156,000 bus rapid transit users and 73,320 women a day, average monthly spending on bus travel fell from NGN 4,120 to NGN 2,141 in 2012 naira, carbon dioxide from vehicles on the corridors fell to 349,000 tonnes a year against a target of 359,000, and 80 per cent of public transport users rated the service satisfactory against a 60 per cent target. One objective indicator was missed: buses carried 458 passengers a day each against a target of 800, which the report puts down to lower demand than expected and to long trips cutting the number of times a seat is reused. The corridor originally chosen, Oshodi–Mile 2–Obalende, was dropped from Bank financing in 2011 after the federal government started incompatible works of its own, and the air-quality monitoring subcomponent was dropped in 2015 because no baseline had been collected before the buses started running. The corridor cost NGN 35.228 billion, about US$226 million, against NGN 11.264 billion or US$88 million at appraisal, a rise of 213 per cent in naira that the report attributes to construction inflation and to the naira falling from 150 to 315 to the dollar; the unit cost works out at US$10.4 million a kilometre. The report puts the economic rate of return at 36 per cent for the infrastructure that took 70 per cent of the financing, against 15 per cent at appraisal, with a net present value of US$486 million over 15 years, the improvement resting partly on a higher value of travel time from a study the transport authority prepared for the analysis. All these figures are the lender's own; no independent check was found.

baoro-bouar-road-house-damage-car.whole: Across the three countries the project rehabilitated 322.2 kilometres of road against a target of 612: 153 of 160 kilometres in the Central African Republic, 109.2 of 320.2 in Cameroon and 60 of 135 in Chad, with 78 per cent of the Central African stretch of the Garoua-Boulaï road in good condition at closing, by the completion report's count. On the Douala–Bangui corridor the average time from a ship being ready to unload to a container reaching its destination was 17.6 days against a target of 27, and the variance in transit time 3.9 against 5.1, while the target of a 20 per cent rise in truck turnarounds was not met, the average reaching 19.2 against a baseline of 15. The 56-kilometre Baoro–Bouar section was still unfinished when the project closed, after 34 months of works against the 20 planned, which the report attributes to the contractor's weak performance, a year lost mobilising equipment, late execution designs for the two main bridges and the road's first 35 kilometres, long delays importing explosives, and then Covid-19 and political turmoil; the rest stops and the Beloko customs platform were also unfinished. The same report's economic table nonetheless marks Baoro–Bouar achieved and puts its cost at US$70.6 million against US$80.4 million at appraisal. No economic rate of return was recalculated for the roads in the Central African Republic, because insecurity made it impossible to collect traffic data; what the report gives instead comes from a survey of users around Bouar and Baoro in April 2021, which reports journeys of 90 minutes from Bouar to Garoua Boulaï and 45 minutes from Bouar to Baoro, about 70 per cent less than in 2007. For the two Cameroon sections where returns were recalculated they were 7.1 and 7.5 per cent, roughly half the appraisal estimates, both with negative net present values. Dabanga–Kousseri, the Kousseri bypass and Nguelendeng–Bongor–Éré–Kélo were not achieved and Magada–Maroua was dropped. US$107.9 million of Bank money was cancelled, US$29.4 million of it the Central African Republic's, and both the report and the Independent Evaluation Group rated the outcome Unsatisfactory, the Group rating efficiency Negligible. All of these figures are the lender's own; no independent check was found.

fenjiang-river-foshan-resettlement.whole: In Foshan the project expanded the Zhen'an wastewater treatment plant from 200,000 to 250,000 cubic metres a day, laid 7.6 kilometres of sewers of the 8 planned, improved 6.7 kilometres of embankment along the Fenjiang river and built three of four decentralised sludge treatment works with a combined 220 tonnes a day, the fourth nearly finished with the client's own money at closing. By the completion report's count the share of Foshan's wastewater collected and treated rose from 55 to 88 per cent and the plant was running at 95 per cent of its hydraulic capacity, serving 600,000 people in Chancheng district. In Jiangmen the Wen Chang Sha plant was expanded from 50,000 to 200,000 cubic metres a day with a pumping station and 22 kilometres of sewers, taking the city's treatment coverage from 22 to 70 per cent and serving about 500,000 people, with the plant at 81 per cent of hydraulic capacity. Against the pollution targets the results are mixed: Foshan removed 1,825 tonnes a year of chemical oxygen demand against a target of 2,500 and 276 tonnes of ammoniacal nitrogen against a target cut from 1,095 to 150, and Jiangmen removed 6,050 tonnes against 14,235 and 917 tonnes against 1,095, the report attributing the shortfalls to the pollution loads in the plants' inflows having been overestimated at appraisal. Unit cash operating costs were not achieved in either city, at RMB 0.63 a cubic metre in Foshan against a target of 0.505 and RMB 0.9 in Jiangmen against 0.556, and Foshan's cost recovery ratio came to 0.9 against a target of 1 in the financial covenant and 1.12 in the results framework, while its debt service ratio was 1.6 against a covenant of 1.3 and a target of 2.33. Work on the client's side of the river embankments, 0.9 kilometres of the 6.67, moved to local financing, 1.1 kilometres of Foshan sewers moved to another locally funded project, and 7 kilometres less of riverbed was dredged after a survey found part of the sediment was clean sand and gravel. No economic rate of return was calculated at appraisal or at completion: the project was assessed on least cost, and the report records that the dredging cost US$20 million more than expected while the river rehabilitation cost less. The report gives the final project cost twice and not identically, as US$142.2 million in the main text and US$147.1 million in the economic section, against US$187.9 million estimated at appraisal, with US$70.92 million of the US$96 million loan disbursed. The environmental management system and a pumping station and pressure pipes in Foshan were still unfinished when the loan closed. All of these figures are the lender's own; no independent check was found.

qiantang-small-town-house-demolition.whole: The project built water treatment and distribution systems in Zhuji and Wucheng, wastewater treatment plants and sewers at Jiande, Qujiang, Youbu and Jianshan, sewer networks in several other towns and the Meicheng sanitary landfill in Jiande. By the completion report's count 397,000 people were served with potable water against a revised target of 360,418; 219,800 people with sanitary solid waste collection and disposal against a revised 202,500; 280,000 tonnes of waste disposal capacity was created against 210,000; 3,974 tonnes a year of chemical oxygen demand was removed against a revised target of 3,907; six operation and maintenance plans were put into use; and tariffs or user fees were introduced in all ten project areas. Two of the pollution targets had been cut before being beaten: total nitrogen removal reached 182 tonnes a year against a target lowered from 239 to 141, and total phosphorus 42 tonnes against a target lowered from 45 to 30, both cut at the mid-term review after the wastewater was found to be less concentrated than assumed. Two works were taken out of the project: 4.3 kilometres of the Panji Road expansion and its networks, cancelled because a provincial highway was delayed and then built with the provincial transport bureau's money, and the Pan'an County Yunshan District sewer networks, dropped when domestic funding became available and built outside the project; the indicator for Yunshan was cancelled with it. US$14.3 million of the loan was left unused and cancelled at closing after competitive bidding and currency movements. The report gives economic rates of return at completion of 33 per cent for the Zhuji water system against 20 at appraisal and 50 per cent for Wucheng against 17, and for the seven wastewater subcomponents it recalculated returns of 20 to 30 per cent against 18 to 28 at appraisal, Yunshan’s 14 per cent not being recalculated after that subcomponent was dropped; it rated efficiency and the overall outcome High and Highly Satisfactory, and the Independent Evaluation Group also rated efficiency High. All of these figures are the lender's own, from its completion report and the Evaluation Group's review of it; no independent check was found.

laibin-water-environment-displacement.whole: The project strengthened 4.63 kilometres of river embankments and slopes, laid 12.18 kilometres of new drainage pipeline and 16.20 kilometres of new sewage pipeline, and set up a flood warning system, a flood emergency plan and flood hazard and risk maps for the city. Each of those met a target that had been cut: embankments from 11.6 kilometres to 4.5, drainage pipeline from 26 kilometres to 12 and sewage pipeline from 21 to 15. By the completion report's count the share of people in the existing urban area at risk from a one-in-50-year river flood fell from 72 per cent to 23, against an appraisal target of 10 per cent, and the area that would be flooded by such an event fell from 30 square kilometres to 8.21, against an appraisal target of 5; direct beneficiaries came to 199,600 against an appraisal figure of 234,000, and 4.17 kilometres of urban area got an improved drainage system against a target of 3. The cuts follow the cancellation of the Longdong river flood works in January 2019, after the municipality changed its land use plan downstream to make room for new development; a low-impact drainage pilot and a technical assistance study on asset management were also cancelled, one sewerage and drainage contract was cancelled, and US$14 million of the loan was cancelled, taking the project cost from US$140.25 million to US$126.25 million. The report puts the economic rate of return at 8.9 per cent at completion on the unit values used at appraisal, against 14.5 per cent at appraisal, and at 13.7 per cent when the values are updated for the rise in land and property prices in Laibin, with a benefit-cost ratio of 1.18 against 1.39 at appraisal; both the report and the Independent Evaluation Group rated efficiency Modest. The report also records that the national anti-corruption authority found serious fraud and corrupt practices by project office and implementing agency staff, prosecuted in the criminal courts in 2017, in the procurement of five civil works contracts signed between 2014 and 2016; the municipality did not promptly inform the Bank, and after an investigation by the Bank's integrity department the Bank declared the contracts in procurement non-compliance in a letter of 12 March 2020. All of these figures are the lender's own; no independent check was found.

corumana-dam-resettlement-mozambique.whole: The project finished the Corumana dam, left without spillway gates since 1989: the saddle dam and main spillway were completed, six spillway gates installed in April and May 2020 after long delays in design, manufacture and delivery, the concrete pillars and abutments repaired, the intake tower equipment rehabilitated, and a dam monitoring system installed. By the completion report's count that raised the reservoir's storage from 720 to 960 million cubic metres, against an appraisal target of 1,240 million that was revised down to 960, and raised the dam's yield by 11.6 million cubic metres a year against an appraisal target of 16.8 million, with bulk water available to greater Maputo rising from 69 to 81 million cubic metres a year once a separate Bank-financed project delivers the treatment and pipes. The dam can only be held at 114 metres above sea level, not the 117 originally planned, until an auxiliary spillway is built, which the report costs at US$40 million and nearly two years; when the report was written in May 2021 the reservoir stood at 109.8 metres, short of the gates. The wider project rehabilitated 50 kilometres of dykes on the Limpopo, protecting about 287,100 people and 45,000 hectares, though to a one-in-20-year flood standard rather than the one-in-50 originally intended, and rehabilitated the Macarretane dam, which supplies about 12,000 producers across 35,000 hectares at Chokwe. Water resources management plans covered 8 river basins against an appraisal target of 19 and a revised target of 12, and the project paid for 3 of them. An integrated water supply system reached 1,095 people against a target of 435, and 660 resettled people got sanitation in their new homes. US$5 million was cancelled at the November 2019 restructuring. The report puts the economic rate of return at 9.9 to 10.4 per cent depending on how the dam is operated, and 9.0 per cent if the auxiliary spillway is never built, against 12.3 per cent at appraisal, and rated efficiency Substantial; the Independent Evaluation Group rated it Modest. All of these figures are the lender's own, from its completion report and the Evaluation Group's review of it; no independent check was found.

ethiopia-sudan-interconnector-line-death.whole: The project built the whole 296.5 kilometres of 230 kV line it set out to build, from Bahir Dar to Metema, upgraded three substations, installed the telecommunications system and saw the Sudanese side of the line finished in June 2010; the full line was commissioned in November 2011, more than a year later than planned. What the line carried fell far short. By the completion report's count Ethiopia exported 175.31 GWh to Sudan against a target of 1,000 GWh, 17.5 per cent, and earned US$8.76 million of foreign exchange against a target of US$50 million, the shortfall coming from five months of exports rather than the two years assumed and from volumes below the levels in the power purchase agreement, after delays the report attributes to a force majeure claim and the Independent Evaluation Group traces to customs clearance at Djibouti, outstanding compensation payments by district administrations that pushed work into the rainy season, and the effect of sanctions on Iran on the Iranian contractor for the substation works. Training of the power corporation's staff was 30 per cent complete, the supervision consultant's contract having ended in December 2010 with no extension, leaving the planned field and overseas training undone. The appraisal document had put the economic rate of return at 48.6 per cent on exports of 832 GWh a year at US$0.055 a kilowatt-hour. Recalculating on actual trade and on an assumption that the price rises to US$0.07 a kilowatt-hour from 2017, the report gives 22 per cent for Ethiopia, 35 per cent for Sudan and 28 per cent for the two together, and both the report and the Evaluation Group rated efficiency Substantial and the outcome Moderately Satisfactory. The loan was 98.3 per cent disbursed. All of these figures are the lender's own; no independent check was found.

gameleira-agrovila-ceara.whole: The programme built reservoirs and canals to hold and move water across Ceará. By the completion report's count the bulk water distributed by the state water company rose from 6.92 to 17.45 cubic metres a second, of which 10.53 is put down to the project; water made available to the Fortaleza metropolitan region rose by 13.21 cubic metres a second against a target of 1.9; water stored in the monitored dams rose by 359.33 million cubic metres; 300,000 people in the interior and 2.6 million in the Fortaleza region were taken out of water rationing; bulk water users rose from 116 to 380; river basin committees rose from 3 to 12 against a target of 11; and the water company covered 100 per cent of its operating costs from 2003, 94 per cent of them from water charges. Several targets were missed: water use permits reached 6,740 against a target of 25,000; in the watershed pilot erosion fell to 20.33 tonnes a hectare a year against a target of 13 from a baseline of 26; water-loss and use-efficiency targets were not measured at all, the report noting the project had no activity aimed at them; and the state water resources secretariat was recorded as not adequately staffed after 2007. Of the eleven reservoirs, six under the first phase and two of the five under the additional financing were finished when the loan closed in December 2011; in mid-December 2012 the Gameleira dam was 75 per cent built, Mamoeiro 92 per cent and Jatobá 96 per cent, and the six pipelines ran from 33 to 95 per cent, with the Itapipoca contract cancelled over the contractor's finances and retendered. The government had agreed to finish the pending works during 2012 and none was finished by mid-December. The report also records that supervision by outside firms was discontinued against the agreement with the Bank, leaving the state groundwater company to supervise all the works. The ex-post economic rate of return for the project as a whole, covering 94 per cent of its cost, was 11 per cent against 14 per cent at appraisal, and for three strategic reservoirs 7 to 15 per cent against 13 to 15 at appraisal, the report putting the difference down to higher investment and operating costs; the overall outcome was rated Moderately Unsatisfactory. All of these figures are the lender's own; no independent check was found.

patna-ganga-riverfront-resettlement.whole: The riverfront works at Patna were the only such investment in the project: a promenade and pedestrian walkway connecting 16 ghats, which the completion report records as fully delivered. Across the project as a whole, by the report's count, 3.74 million people were direct beneficiaries against a revised target of 3.57 million; 17,450 tonnes a year of biochemical oxygen demand was abated against a revised target of 16,500 and an appraisal target of 21,000; 404 million litres a day of untreated wastewater was kept out of the Ganga against a revised 386 and an appraisal 270; and 317,647 households were connected to sewerage against a revised target of 325,000 and an appraisal target of 475,310. Five of six programme institutions were judged to be set up and working: the exception is the Bihar unit, where the report records over half the sanctioned posts vacant and poor performance in procurement, financial management and safeguards. Sixty real-time water quality monitoring stations were running against a revised target of 70. US$60.7 million was cancelled at the sixth restructuring, and the closing date was put back two years. The report puts the economic rate of return across the investments at 35.21 per cent with a benefit-cost ratio of 6.22 and a net present value of INR 140.80 billion at a 10 per cent discount rate, and for the Patna riverfront alone at 39.92 per cent, on costs of INR 206.39 crore against benefits of INR 1,908.26 crore; the appraisal document calculated no overall return because the investments had not been chosen, giving instead 13 to 32 per cent for generic sewage treatment plants. The Independent Evaluation Group rated efficiency Substantial and the outcome Satisfactory. The riverfront benefit figure rests in part on an estimate of increased economic activity made for the report, and every figure here is the lender's own; no independent check was found.

newmap-nigeria-erosion-displacement.whole: The project treated gully complexes and other erosion sites across 20 states. By the completion report's count 92 sites were treated with all of their planned measures against a revised target of 55 and an appraisal target of 30, and 103 sites had their erosion severity reduced against the same targets, with 11 of those sites more than half finished rather than complete at closing; 57 of the works were erosion control, 16 flood control and 30 both, and 54 were urban, 16 semi-urban and 29 rural. It records 2,164 hectares brought under bioremediation against a target of 400, net greenhouse gas emissions reduced by 149,554 tonnes of carbon dioxide equivalent a year against a target of 2,411, that figure being 198,908 tonnes from afforestation and 93,284 from solar power set against 142,618 tonnes from the construction work, nearly 200,000 people trained, 396 community interest groups assisted, 116 hydrological and meteorological stations installed for flood early warning, and three national and eight state institutions on erosion and watershed management set up. Its figure for land under sustainable landscape management is given twice and not identically: 27,593 hectares in the text and 30,627.96 in the results framework, against a target of 400; the same 30,627.96 is also the figure the framework gives for land treated for erosion, against a target of 20,000. The project cost US$908 million after additional financing, with US$665.94 million in the works component, which the report divides by the 92 completed sites to give an average of US$7.25 million a site. The report's cost-benefit analysis at completion gives an economic rate of return of 15 per cent with a net present value of US$317 million and a benefit-cost ratio of 1.4 over 2013 to 2022 at a 10 per cent discount rate, against 12 per cent, US$44 million and 1.1 at appraisal in 2012 over 2013 to 2042 at the same rate, and against 16 per cent and US$540 million in the 2019 analysis, which used a 6 per cent rate and ran to 2047; the later analyses count benefits the 2012 one did not, including avoided displacement, afforestation, emission reductions and the rise in the value of land that had been erosion-prone. The report rated efficiency Substantial. All of these figures are the lender's own; no independent check was found.

nepal-raidp-land-donation.whole: The project upgraded 1,740 kilometres of dry-season road to all-season standard against a revised target of 1,165 and an appraisal target of 800, the completion report putting the overshoot down to savings from exchange rates and from lower bids after e-bidding was introduced. It supported 745 trail bridges against a revised target of 317 — 164 built in full and 581 fabricated — maintained about 4,600 kilometres of road a year against a revised target of 4,500, updated district transport master plans in 25 districts of the 30 targeted, and ran e-bidding in 74 district development committees and 17 municipalities against a target of nine districts. It fell short on trails: 141 kilometres of rural trail were upgraded to dry-season standard against a revised target of 211, about 30 per cent short, the report saying the figure excludes length that overlapped between work packages. Two of the four accessibility indicators were recorded as not achieved, the share of people in the terai districts living within two hours' walk of an all-season road rising by less than the 10 per cent targeted in both the original and the new districts, while the hill districts met or nearly met their 15 per cent targets. Motorised trips by beneficiaries rose 145 per cent and non-motorised trips 77 per cent against a 20 per cent target, and travel times fell 48 and 35 per cent against a 20 per cent target, both measured against a 2011 study used in place of the 2005 baseline, which had covered motorised trips only; the traffic indicator could not be settled because the figures collected were daily rather than annual averages. A January 2014 cost-benefit study of a sample of upgraded roads gave an average first-year economic rate of return of 28 per cent, above the 12 per cent benchmark, with a net present value of US$8.6 million for the programme, and found cost per beneficiary within the US$100 ceiling and mostly at US$50 or below; the Independent Evaluation Group notes that the ceiling itself was arbitrary. Upgrading cost about US$23,157 a kilometre on the original roads and US$23,382 on the additional ones, and trail bridges about US$390 a metre of span. All of these figures are the lender's own; no independent check was found.

ouagadougou-onea-works-before-compensati.whole: The project installed 86,832 new household water connections against a target of 82,170 and built or rehabilitated 349 public standpipes against a target of 186, which by the completion report's count brought 848,000 people improved water against a target of 759,000; 615,125 of them are in Ouagadougou, about 23 per cent of the city on 2020 population estimates. It reports 437,237 people reaching improved on-site sanitation against a target of 351,600, through 49,686 household latrines against a target of 40,000 and 59,545 sumps, and 120,666 pupils through 352 blocks of seven school latrines, 308 of them in Ouagadougou, with 285 schools also connected to the water network. Two faecal sludge treatment plants were built, one in each city, and the report says the investments doubled the country's water production capacity; staff per thousand connections at the water utility fell from 4.3 to 3.5. After procurement delays in hiring the connection contractors, the utility installed 7,442 of the connections itself in 2017 and 2018, counted as counterpart funding. The report puts the economic rate of return at 14.5 per cent at completion, covering 79 per cent of project cost, against 16.8 per cent at appraisal covering 62 per cent, with a net present value of US$20.12 million at a 10 per cent discount rate, and the financial rate of return for the utility at 10.2 per cent against 13.6 per cent at appraisal; it attributes the falls to the cost of the transmission reinforcement added with the additional financing, which does not increase water sales at once. It rated efficiency High. The Independent Evaluation Group rated efficiency Substantial and the outcome Satisfactory, and states that the health and time savings counted in the 14.5 per cent were estimates rather than figures measured by a survey or an impact evaluation, so the method behind the rate was not robust. All of these figures are the lender's own, from its completion report and the Evaluation Group's review of it; no independent check was found.
